narration: You got your first job offer, it felt a little low, but you said yes to get experience. That one number just locked in a tax on your entire career.
visual: Person silhouette receiving an offer letter that drops in from above. A heavy chain-anchor appears below, connected to the letter with chain links.

narration: Here's the trap — raises are almost always a percentage of what you already make. Start low, every raise stays low. The gap compounds every single year.
visual: Side-by-side bar chart for Year 1, Year 10, Year 20. Market Rate bars (amber) versus Underpaid bars (gray) show a widening gap.

narration: Start just $5,000 below market at 22, and over a 30-year career, that one gap compounds into $347,000 out of your pocket. Wild, right?
visual: Giant amber counter counting up to $347,000. Age timeline below runs from 22 to 60 with amber fill growing across it.

narration: And 72% of employers base your new offer on what you already make. So if you're underpaid now, that anchor just follows you to your next job.
visual: Office desk scene with boss figure passing an offer letter to employee. An anchor drops below the letter connected by chain links.

narration: Workers who job-hop every two to three years earn 50% more over their lifetime. Each switch resets the anchor to market rate — that's the actual fix.
visual: Three buildings at increasing heights representing Jobs 1, 2, 3. Person silhouette jumps between them. Salary labels ($60K, $78K, $95K) above each building.

narration: Only 37% of people negotiate their very first offer. One conversation can recover $5,000 to $10,000. That gap takes 30 years to close otherwise — start negotiating now.
visual: Handshake between two figures. Small money bag (before) next to large amber money bag (after). Bold CTA box: ASK ONCE = $347K.
